name: Benjamin Gevercer
title: Senior Associate, Olson Remcho LLP
background: Gevercer holds a B.A., cum laude, from the University of California, Santa Cruz, and a J.D. from the University of California, Davis School of Law, where he served as an Articles Editor of the U.C. Davis Law Review and co-chaired the King Hall Legal Foundation. He was admitted to the California bar in November 2018. Before law school he worked on presidential campaigns in Pennsylvania and North Carolina, and he later worked at the California Department of Finance on matters including 2011 Public Safety Realignment, public safety funding, and the economic review of regulations. (Source: Olson Remcho LLP attorney biography.)

As a senior associate at Olson Remcho LLP, a Sacramento-based political and government law firm, Gevercer practices in election law litigation, constitutional matters, and public policy disputes, with particular focus, per his firm biography, on 'drafting complex ballot measures at both the state and local level.' He has written on California's initiative process and fiscal constitution, with work published in the Southern California Law Review and through the California Constitution Center, and belongs to the Sacramento County Bar Association, the Leonard M. Friedman Bar Association, the Schwartz-Levi American Inn of Court, and the California Political Attorneys Association. (Source: Olson Remcho LLP attorney biography.)

Gevercer is a co-proponent, alongside California Teachers Association president David B. Goldberg, of Proposition 3 on the November 2026 California ballot, which deletes the scheduled 2031 expiration of the Proposition 30/Proposition 55 personal income tax surcharge on the state's top three tax brackets. The two filed the initiative with the Attorney General on August 29, 2025; Olson Remcho is listed as the measure's contact firm in the Attorney General's filing, and the pair were cleared to begin collecting petition signatures on November 4, 2025. (Source: content/measures/ca-prop-3-2026.json in this voter guide; California Secretary of State initiative-circulation notice for the measure.)
